correctness.rationale: The level indicator is half of 1+(-1)^{epsilon+Q}. Expanding its two translates and using the nonsingular polar form gives the stated four-term Walsh sum; the two Gauss terms cancel when b(a)=1. The real symmetric Weyl directions are exactly b(a)=0, with Frobenius norm sqrt(N); their intensity responses are distinct Walsh characters on the N² orbit indices, giving eigenvalues N|A(a,b)/K|². At nonzero shift each symmetric frequency set has N/2 elements, with two singled out. At m=1 and rho=-1 the seed is a point mass, so only the four diagonal directions survive; at rho=+1 the seed has size three, with overlap two at nonzero shift and nontrivial zero-shift Walsh modulus one, giving condition number three. For m≥2 the smallest ambiguity modulus is h. The sphere's projector normal operator is scalar on the traceless part with value 2N/(N+2); the two nontrivial symmetric sectors agree only when L=h, giving N=16 and K=6 and exactly the claimed fourth moment. The frozen checks/verify.py was located and inspected, not executed. A minor literature-comparison caveat is that the m=1 singleton has difference-set parameter zero; it is not ruled out by the numerical small-intersection threshold alone, though the cited cyclic theorem is about a different group and its indicator hypothesis is not an injectivity argument for the singleton.
